review_scope: All 74 definitions and all 9 semantic relations were read, including explanation, scope, applicability, log context, cannot_infer, evidence and value_semantics. Important and doubtful claims were checked against the primary documents listed below. No runtime, catalog, or core batch file was edited by this reviewer.

reviewed_relations.notes: HKCC is the predefined alias of the current hardware-profile branch.
HKCR incorporates machine Classes registrations along with the applicable user Classes registrations.
HKCU maps to a concrete user branch represented by the UserHive schema; the template is not itself a runtime target.
An extension default value can name the ProgID represented by the ProgID schema.
When present, a CLSID subkey in a COM-oriented ProgID registration maps that textual identifier to a class; this is not a requirement for every Shell file-association ProgID.
A concrete class can associate with an AppID registration through its AppID metadata.
ProviderOrder names resolve to provider-specific registrations beneath Services.
Setup classes group installation configuration; interface classes describe exposed device functionality. These are distinct identities.
The WMI environment documentation separates system variables from per-user hive variables.

findings.issue: The generic service/driver node describes ImagePath only as a binary path. This is incomplete for Win32 services: the registry value can also carry launch arguments. An external consumer could treat the complete launch string as a literal file path or discard arguments that materially change service configuration. The cited driver-tree description alone does not cover that broader service launch-string interpretation.
findings.observed_text: Path to the registered service or driver binary.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the driver binary-path convention separately from Win32 service executable path plus optional command-line arguments; require preservation of the complete raw string and applicable service type when interpreting it. Add Service Entry Point and CreateService primary evidence.

findings.issue: The meaning correctly says REG_MULTI_SZ DLL names but omits the source’s explicit detail that these names exclude the .dll extension. This is a precision improvement for future value interpretation, rather than an incorrect key/value classification.
findings.observed_text: REG_MULTI_SZ list of registered SSP/AP DLL names.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify DLL base names without the .dll extension, separated by NUL characters in REG_MULTI_SZ; retain the current limit that this documentation covers SSP/AP registration rather than every SSP mechanism.
source_sections: Registering SSP/AP DLLs / introductory registration value description

findings.issue: The coinstaller note says applicability depends on package model and mechanism but does not mention explicit Microsoft deprecation of class installers/co-installers. The current wording is cautious and the namespace role is correct, but a training note should expose this lifecycle limit as clearly as the adjacent hardware-profile notes do.
findings.observed_text: This is the documented class-coinstaller namespace; applicability depends on the driver package model and installation mechanism in use.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the documented deprecation caveat with the new primary source. Do not invent a universal Windows release where the registry key stopped existing or all coinstallers ceased working.
